title: Si Bien: Granting a Point in Chile's Recent History

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *si bien* from B2 Unit 8: it means "although it is true that", takes the indicative and belongs to formal writing, such as reports and news. First you grant a true point, then you say what matters more. Recent Chilean history is full of such pairs: a vote that was won but did not change everything at once, or a text that was rejected while the process went on.

sections.title: Si bien and what matters more
rows: Si bien el plebiscito de 1988 lo ganó el No, Pinochet siguió en el cargo hasta 1990.
Although the No won the 1988 plebiscite, Pinochet stayed in office until 1990.
Si bien el estallido empezó por el metro, las protestas pedían más cambios.
Although the outburst began over the metro, the protests asked for more changes.
Si bien los chilenos votaron por una nueva constitución en 2020, rechazaron el primer texto en 2022.
Although Chileans voted for a new constitution in 2020, they rejected the first draft in 2022.
La transición, si bien fue pacífica, dejó temas pendientes.
The transition, although peaceful, left open issues. (in the middle, between commas)

items.spanish: Si bien la dictadura terminó en 1990, el debate sobre ese pasado continúa.
items.english: Although the dictatorship ended in 1990, the debate about that past continues.

items.spanish: Si bien el segundo texto también fue rechazado, el proceso constitucional terminó.
items.english: Although the second draft was also rejected, the constitutional process ended.

items.spanish: Si bien muchos votaron, otros no fueron a las urnas.
items.english: Although many voted, others did not go to the polls.

sections.content: *Si bien* takes the indicative and no *que*: *si bien fue*, not *si bien que fue* and not *si bien fuera*. It is two words: do not confuse it with *sí* (yes) or *si* (if). In everyday speech say *aunque*.
